title: Finite separable algebraic subextension of a finitely generated field extension
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $k'\subseteq K$ be the subfield consisting of elements separably algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then $K/k'$ is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and $k'/k$ is finite.

proof.text: By the definition of the relative separable closure [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], k' is a subfield of K containing k and k'/k is separable algebraic. Let F be the separable algebraic closure of k' in K; by the same definition, applied to the extension K/k', F is a subfield of K containing k' and F/k' is separable algebraic. The separable-permanence theorem [lem-zl-separable-permanence], applied to the tower k ⊆ k' ⊆ F, shows that F/k is separable algebraic. So every element of F is separably algebraic over k and lies in k' by the definition of k'; hence F = k'. Thus every element of K that is separably algebraic over k' belongs to k'. The implication (2) ⇒ (1) of the equivalence [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-separable], applied to K/k', proves that K/k' is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: Let k_alg be the algebraic closure of k in K. The finite-generation hypothesis and Fields Tag 037J give [k_alg : k] < infinity [lem-zl-finite-algebraic-closure]. Since every element of k' is algebraic over k, k' is an intermediate subfield of k_alg/k; a subfield of a finite-dimensional k-vector space is finite-dimensional over k. Hence [k' : k] is finite.
